clue.text: Switch to compliant tone, showing consideration

indicators.note: to switch things around is to change their positions, so the letters that follow get rearranged

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone adopts a more agreeable manner of speaking to show they are being considerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemplation is careful, thoughtful reflection on something, a direct synonym for giving it consideration.

clue.text: Effective employee

blocks.note: first meaning: in force, functioning, as a law that is now in effect
second meaning: a worker, especially one in a factory or a secret agent

explanation.surface: An appraisal phrase praising a capable member of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means functioning or in force; as a noun it names a worker or a secret agent.

clue.text: Start to reorder pastries

indicators.note: reordering means putting the letters of the preceding word into a different sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin ordering more baked goods from the bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like a verb meaning begin, but it is simply the five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarts are open pies of pastry with a sweet or savoury filling, so they are examples of pastries.

clue.text: With team in disarray before games, one included something to eat

indicators.note: a squad in disarray is disorganised, so its letters fall out of their usual order
something included is held inside another, so the single letter goes within the games abbreviation

blocks.note: the four letters of team rearranged
PE, physical education, is school games
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A disorganised sports side heads to their matches, with one player squeezed in.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is the school subject physical education, often just called games in Britain; I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat pie is a savoury pastry filled with meat, a vague but fair example of something to eat.

clue.text: Means of communicating with landlords?

blocks.note: first meaning: written messages sent by post
second meaning, read whimsically: people who let out property, hence those who let

explanation.surface: A question about how tenants should get in touch with the owners of their flats.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful coinage: one who lets property is a 'letter', which the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence by post is a means of communicating, and landlords are, jokingly, people who let rooms.

clue.text: Noble woman comes back for proof of ownership

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the woman's name is read from right to left

blocks.note: a noble person holds a title such as duke or countess
Dee is a woman's name, short for Deirdre or Dorothy

explanation.surface: An aristocratic lady returns home to claim her property, papers in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble woman' reads as one person, a lady of rank, but the two words are separate pieces; the answer is two words, the first losing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal document proving that someone owns a piece of land or property.

clue.text: Had pained expression as end unfolded

indicators.note: something unfolded is opened out and laid in a new shape, so the letters of the last word move around

blocks.note: ow is the cry of someone hurt
the three letters of end rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grimaced as the ending of a story played out.
explanation.definitionFit: To have owned something is to have possessed it, so the past tense means had.

clue.text: Private sign

blocks.note: surface reading: a secret gesture or signal shared between two people
setter's reading: the word written on a notice at the edge of land closed to the public, and what such a notice warns

explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective meaning secret, but it is what a notice on a gate says, and another notice saying the same thing is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice warning strangers to keep off land announces that the property is private and not open to walkers.

clue.text: Many take refuge in a lie to survive turbulent conditions

indicators.note: taking refuge in a place means sheltering inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a story is a fib or untruth
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so a large number
to weather something is to come through it intact

explanation.surface: In hard times a crowd of people shelter behind a falsehood just to get by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives a single letter because the Roman numeral for a thousand stands for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather literally means wild wind and rain, and figuratively a period of trouble or difficulty.

clue.text: Respond in an extreme way to crumpled cover with tear

indicators.note: crumpled paper is crushed out of shape, so the letters of the two words lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flies off the handle at a book jacket that has got creased and ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to show a response out of proportion to its cause, an emotional excess.

clue.text: Reversible doctrine

indicators.note: something reversible works just as well turned round, so the word wanted reads the same backwards as forwards

blocks.note: the definition, which happens to read identically in both directions

explanation.surface: A belief system that can be turned inside out, like a two-sided coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible' seems to say the belief can be abandoned; instead it describes the spelling, which reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held by a group, one article of a doctrine or creed.

clue.text: Gathers spare change

indicators.note: change here is a verb telling the solver to alter the arrangement of the letters before it

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone collects the loose coins left over in their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare change' reads as loose coins, but change is the instruction and spare the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut and collect a crop at harvest, so it means gathers in.

clue.text: He claims to be an actor

blocks.note: first meaning: a claimant, especially to a throne
second meaning: one who pretends, as a performer does on stage

explanation.surface: A man asserts that he works on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old and Young Pretenders were Stuart claimants to the British throne, which is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is a claimant to a title or crown, and also literally someone who puts on a false show.

clue.text: One point victory led to reform by cheat

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it again in a new shape, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

blocks.note: south is one of the compass points
a win is a victory
the three letters of led rearranged

explanation.surface: A narrow win prompted a cheat to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One point victory' reads as a narrow win, but one point is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a fraudulent scheme to get money dishonestly, so the noun means a cheat or con.

clue.text: Rude to turn and endlessly single out people''s homes

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so it is read from its last letter
without an end means the final letter of the next word is cut off
out suggests the letters are knocked out of place and need rearranging

blocks.note: lewd means crude or obscene
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told it is bad manners to whirl round and pick out particular people's houses.
explanation.walkthrough: LEWD read backwards is DWEL; SINGLE loses its E and the rest is shuffled to LINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwellings are the places where people live, a formal word for houses, flats and other homes.

clue.text: Pleasingly, we adapted with style

indicators.note: something adapted has been modified into a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple adjusted to their surroundings with charm and flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Done sweetly means done in a pleasant, charming or agreeable way, an adverb matching pleasingly.

clue.text: Revolution regarding sudden change in policy

blocks.note: one revolution of a wheel is one turn
about means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: A political uprising over a government's abrupt U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests politics, matching the surface, but here it is one rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnabout is an abrupt reversal of opinion or position, as when a government abandons a stance.

clue.text: Little Leslie was inside a long time, though still looking young

indicators.note: being inside something means being enclosed by it, so the short name sits within the other word

blocks.note: ages is a long time
Les is the short form of the name Leslie

explanation.surface: A man called Leslie served a long prison sentence but somehow still looks youthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was inside' suggests a prison term, which fits the surface, but it only signals one piece going within another.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless describes someone who never seems to grow older, retaining a youthful appearance over the years.

clue.text: It's not a strange place to start a journey

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the preceding letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a familiar starting point for travel is nothing unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a denial, but 'It's not a' are the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway or bus station is where travellers board, so it is a typical departure point for a trip.

clue.text: Finish with terribly sore back

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters of the next word are badly jumbled

blocks.note: to finish is to end
the four letters of sore rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ends the day with an aching back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sore back' reads as an ailment, but back is the definition, a verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or proposal is to give it public approval and support, which is to back it.

clue.text: Grant one the right, not being heartless, to mingle with elite

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word before is taken out
mingling mixes things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone without compassion is barred from mixing with high society.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT loses its middle O to leave NT, which is mixed with ELITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them a legal or moral claim to something, granting them a right.

clue.text: Begging to take the place of one within

indicators.note: within means inside, so the numeral is placed inside the longer word

blocks.note: to supplant is to replace or oust
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to stand in for another person.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside SUPPLANT, between the L and the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppliant is an adjective for someone humbly asking or pleading, so it fits begging.

clue.text: Gasp with cry of surprise at show

blocks.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
O is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An audience member gasps and shrieks during a theatre performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto, short for pantomime, is a British Christmas stage show for families with slapstick and audience shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a comic theatrical entertainment, so it is a kind of show.

clue.text: Treatise on land area

blocks.note: first meaning: a short essay or pamphlet, often religious or political
second meaning: a stretch of territory

explanation.surface: The title of a scholarly essay about geography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' reads as 'about' in a book title, but it simply joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a written pamphlet arguing a case and an expanse of land.

clue.text: Sailor returning to card game

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the small word is read backwards

blocks.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman goes back to a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is played with a special pack of cards and is a traditional card game in parts of Europe, besides its use in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Dash indoors after quarrel?

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: to hurry inside
second meaning: an argument or brush with someone

explanation.surface: Someone hurries inside after an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an informal word for a disagreement or clash, and to run in is to rush inside.

clue.text: Intervene when no respite is arranged

indicators.note: arranging means putting in order, so the letters before are set out afresh

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A mediator steps in once it is clear there will be no break in the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to put oneself between parties in a dispute, which means to step in or mediate.

clue.text: He gets us into a new residential area

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the letters are rebuilt in a different order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of these five words

explanation.surface: An estate agent finds a family a place in a newly built neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a housing estate is a planned development of homes built together, often by a council.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a group of houses built as a single development, so it is a residential area.
